questions.prompt: A legacy `BillingApi.GetRowsAsXml()` must satisfy the new `IDataSource.FetchRecords()` — neither side may be modified. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Adapter** signal: INCOMPATIBLE INTERFACES, neither modifiable — the adapter realizes the Target interface and WRAPS the Adaptee, converting calls. (Facade would simplify, not convert.)

questions.prompt: Folders contain files AND folders; `GetSize()` must work identically on a single file or a whole tree. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Composite** signal: PART-WHOLE TREE + UNIFORM treatment of leaf and group. The heart of the code: the composite's operation loops `foreach (child) child.SameOperation()`.

questions.prompt: `LeaveHomeMode()` is one simple call that internally coordinates lights, thermostat, locks and camera APIs. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Facade** signal: ONE SIMPLIFIED ENTRY POINT over a COMPLEX SUBSYSTEM. No interface mismatch (that's Adapter) — just complexity reduction.

questions.prompt: When a stock price changes, ALL registered dashboards update automatically; the price object doesn't know the concrete dashboards. Pattern?
questions.explain: **Observer** signal: ONE-TO-MANY automatic notification on state change. Mechanics: Subject keeps a list of IObserver, **Attach/Detach/Notify**; Notify fires inside the state setter and calls every observer's **Update**.

questions.prompt: Order the Observer subject's flow when its state changes:
questions.explain: Notify lives **in the Subject** and fires inside the setter only when state ACTUALLY changes; it loops the observer list calling the contract method **Update**. (Drill Q11's exact missing lines.)

questions.prompt: In Composite, the composite class's `ReadData()` contains `foreach (var s in _sensors) s.ReadData();` while the leaf's just reads its own value. Why is the foreach 'the heart' of the pattern?
options: The composite delegates the SAME operation recursively to every child — uniformity is what lets clients ignore leaf vs group
It is faster than a for loop
questions.explain: Uniform recursion = the whole point: clients call ReadData() on ANY node; trees of any depth respond correctly. Leaf methods that can't apply (AddSensor on a leaf) throw NotImplementedException in the drill's variant.

questions.prompt: Flight status boards, mobile apps and gate displays all update THE MOMENT a flight changes; one display is a vendor panel exposing only `PushText(string)`. Which TWO patterns?
options: Observer (one-to-many updates) + Adapter (VendorXAdapter realizes IDisplay and wraps PushText)
questions.explain: 'ALL update the moment it changes' = **Observer** (FlightStatus = Subject; displays = observers behind IDisplay). The vendor panel's incompatible `PushText(string)` needs an **Adapter** that implements `IDisplay.Render(FlightInfo)` and converts: `_panel.PushText(Format(info))`.

questions.prompt: Adapter vs Facade — the one-line distinction:
options: Adapter CONVERTS an incompatible interface; Facade SIMPLIFIES a complex but compatible subsystem
Adapter is for UIs, Facade for databases
Facade converts types, Adapter hides complexity
questions.explain: Ask: is there an interface MISMATCH (→ Adapter) or just TOO MANY calls to make (→ Facade)? Exam questions hinge on this exact distinction.
